title: Underwriting Rule: Number of Rental Buildings per Landlord (LandlordGuard)
content:
**Rule.** A landlord may insure up to 12 rental buildings under the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy, one LandlordGuard policy per building address, counted across every dwelling policy in the customer's name. A live policy is one that is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal.

**Condition of binding.** No other LandlordGuard dwelling policy that is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal covers the same property address.

## Basis of the address condition

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| What is compared | the property address of the building to be bound against the property address on each other dwelling policy |
| Which policies count | only those whose status is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal |
| Whose word decides | the carrier's policy records, as they stand before the policy is bound |
| Result when such a policy exists | the address already has its one LandlordGuard policy |

A cancelled or expired LandlordGuard policy at the same address is not in any of the four listed statuses, so it does not stand in the way of a new policy at that address.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A landlord holds eleven live LandlordGuard policies on eleven addresses and asks to insure a twelfth building at a new address. The twelfth building is within the limit of 12 and no live policy covers that address.
2. A landlord's policy on 14 Elm Street is pending nonrenewal. A second LandlordGuard policy on 14 Elm Street is not bound, because a live policy already covers that address.
3. A landlord's earlier policy on 22 Oak Avenue expired last year. The expired policy is not live and does not block a new policy on 22 Oak Avenue.
